_governance.statement: The network pays the data center a fence price per MWh of heat it takes (Con Ed pilot: $26/MMBtu = $88.7/MWh).
_governance.open_question: Price for 111 8th tenants to be negotiated (A06 19.5 / 26 / 31.5)

_governance.statement: Users pay a usage rate per MWh plus a fixed annual connection charge (pilot: $26.63/MMBtu + $5,000/yr, subsidised).
_governance.open_question: Unsubsidised level for a larger network

_governance.statement: A fully cost-based rate would be $151.93 per MBH of heat-exchanger capacity vs $0.12 in the pilot: scale is needed for cost recovery.
Standard multi-tenant heat contract at 111 8th: any tenant cooling plant can sell heat on the same terms (Term 2).
Pilot costs are recovered across Con Ed ratepayers (bill impact +0.06% electric, +0.23% gas).
_governance.open_question: Whether a scaled network keeps ratepayer recovery

_governance.statement: Federal ITC does not apply to non-geothermal heat-recovery projects (Con Ed finding): financing must come from rates, grants or developers.
A regulated utility (Con Ed, under UTENJA) owns and operates the loop and energy-centre equipment.
_governance.open_question: Who owns an expansion beyond the 5-year pilot

_governance.statement: NYCHA owns the buildings; PACT partners (Related, Essence) manage the campus.
The source building owner keeps its cooling plant and sells heat at the fence; heat-recovery interfaces funded by the network or by tenants (DC_funding).
Rebuild developer delivers heat-ready plant rooms and 45 C distribution in each new tower (Term 3).
_governance.open_question: Design team commitment before design freeze

_governance.statement: The operator decides when the network accepts heat from the source.
The source commits a monthly minimum of heat; its revenue is reduced for any shortfall.
Customers commit a minimum purchase; shortfall compensation is capped.
The data center keeps its cooling towers; the network never becomes part of its cooling (the pilot rejects heat to the source only ~10 h/yr).
Backup heat: existing steam/boilers (pilot adds a steam heat exchanger and keeps the radiators); electric boilers in rebuilt towers.
Monitoring and public reporting (pilot budgets ~$1M for metrics); our Term 5 adds a public dashboard of heat, CO2 and combustion displaced.
Data-center heat unavailable or a tenant leaves: backup sized to the full peak; several tenants under one contract.
Rebuild demolishes connected buildings: the pilot keeps $19M of reusable infrastructure and the connected block is rebuilt last.
_governance.open_question: Transition plan from S3 to S3R

_governance.statement: Affordability: the pilot nets Fulton only +$1k/yr, so tariffs must keep NYCHA bills at or below today (H6).
Source operations can change the heat price: 85 10th Ave cut chiller use and the needed price rose ~25%.
Urban construction costs (test pits on Manhattan streets) exceeded expectations: 15% contingency.
Contract horizon: data centers plan ~10 years and pilot agreements last 5 years, shorter than network assets (25 yr).
Exit cost if the network ends: pilot decommissioning estimated at $13.3M.
Data centers face growing opposition nationally (25+ projects cancelled); visible community benefit matters.
Pilot practice: residents engaged and building managers compensated for design review.
Rebuild: 94% of households stay in place during construction; the project is contested, so the network should fit whatever is built.
_governance.open_question: Resident views on the network itself

_governance.statement: NYC precedent (FPCJ / Verizon): NYSERDA and NYC EDC support; the heat source insisted on redundancy.
Visible air-quality benefit: Chelsea PM2.5 9.5 vs 6.3 ug/m3 citywide; combustion displaced is reported.
An operating pilot loop already runs on the same block (85 10th Ave -> Fulton) with valves for future connections; Google (111 8th) has expressed interest.
Rebuild timing: first move-ins end of 2028; new buildings use electric/renewable heating, so they can be designed heat-ready now.
Baseline is Con Ed steam (Fulton, 111 8th) and gas boilers (Elliott-Chelsea, Chelsea Market).
The site and Fulton are in a state-designated disadvantaged tract (LMI 80%).
LL97 fines do not apply to NYCHA (pilot filing); LL97 motivates only the commercial offtakers.
Manhattan grid: Zone J winter peak 7.55 GW; the pilot raised the customer winter peak by 320 kW.
Value to the data center: heat revenue minus added electricity and O&M; own steam/gas displaced (S1); social licence (qualitative).
Value to heat users: bill change per building and per apartment, continuity, in-unit cooling where added (pilot: 36 apartments).
Value to the community: CO2 avoided, local NOx avoided, low-income households served, winter peak effect.
